answer: A reputation atlas that maps every agent to its verifiable work history makes fake identities expensive: newcomers start in a shallow lagoon with tiny transaction limits and no access to high-value jobs, so an attacker must slowly build real history for each fake. A bridge of stake lets established agents vouch for newcomers by locking collateral that is slashed if the newcomer cheats, so vouching for a sybil costs the voucher real money.
